profile.summary: GFMBench-API is a Python interface that puts many existing genomic benchmarks behind one evaluation API. A model implements a small set of inference methods, and the library then runs it on 22 tasks covering supervised sequence and variant classification and zero-shot variant effect prediction, writing one CSV of task and metric rows. It is for comparing genomic foundation models without rewriting a pipeline per benchmark.

summary_quotes.text: GFMBench-API is an extensible benchmarking suite for assessing genomic foundation models (GFMs) across a diverse set of downstream tasks, including classification, variant effect prediction, and zero-shot evaluation.
GFMBench-API supports evaluation on **22 unique tasks**, grouped as:
Simply implement the methods below in your model class; inheritance is **not** required.
Results are auto-saved in a single CSV with this schema:

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Two families of task. Supervised classification and variant prediction: promoter, splice site and transcription factor binding from GUE; coding, non-coding, expression, common versus rare, methylation QTL and splicing QTL variant classification from VariantBenchmarks; causal eQTL, enhancer and histone mark tasks from the Long Range Benchmark. Zero-shot variant effect prediction: ClinVar SNVs by embedding distance and by likelihood, ClinVar insertions and deletions, BEND expression and disease effects, BRCA1 functional impact, TraitGym complex and Mendelian variants, LRB pathogenic OMIM variants and LOL-EVE causal eQTL indels.

quotes.text: | GuePromoterAllTask                | Binary classification of promoter vs non-promoter DNA sequences. |
| VariantBenchmarksMEQTLTask           | Binary classification of variants affecting DNA methylation rates. |
| LRBHistoneMarksTask                  | Multi-label classification of genomic bins across 20 histone-mark tracks. |
| SonglabClinvarTask                | Zero-shot pathogenicity prediction for ClinVar SNVs using likelihood-based scoring. |
| TraitGymMendelianTask             | Zero-shot prediction of Mendelian disease-associated variants. |

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: The tasks wrap data from existing benchmarks rather than new data collection. All task data sit under one root directory, one subdirectory per task named after the task class, holding train.csv, dev.csv and test.csv; missing files are downloaded automatically on first use. Classification data carry a sequence and a label; variant effect data carry a reference sequence, an alternative sequence and a label. Sequences use A, T, C, G, N and P for padding at chromosome boundaries, and are upper-cased. The NOTICE states that the downloaded third-party data include datasets with non-commercial terms.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: A model supplies inference methods by duck typing: sequence to label probabilities, variant and reference pairs to label probabilities, sequence to regression outputs, sequence to per-nucleotide probabilities and embeddings, a position mapping helper, and masked-position token probabilities. Any method a model does not implement can return None and the metrics that need it are skipped. Supervised classification tasks compute accuracy, MCC, AUROC and AUPRC. Zero-shot SNV tasks add cosine similarity AUROC and AUPRC between variant and reference embeddings at the variant position, and AUROC and AUPRC on the masked-token log-likelihood ratio. Tasks expose eval_test_set, eval_validation_set and eval_cross_validation_fold, and results go to a CSV with one row per task and metric and one column per model name, with NO_RESULTS where a result is missing.

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: Install your model's own dependencies first, then the library's basic_requirements.txt on top, and run usage_examples/run_benchmark.py with a model key. Flags select linear probing, the number of fine-tuning epochs, the output CSV path and the inference cache size. A sanity check mode runs on 100-sample subsets. If a model's dependencies clash with the benchmark stack, the model can run in a separate Python environment and process behind a thin adapter.

facts.value: 22 tasks wrapping data from GUE, VariantBenchmarks, the Long Range Benchmark, BEND, TraitGym, the SongLab ClinVar set, BRCA1, VEP-eval, LOL-EVE and a ClinVar indel task. The README gives no example counts per task.

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: Fixed files per task: train.csv, dev.csv and test.csv in the task's data directory. Supervised tasks return train, validation and test datasets; zero-shot tasks return a test dataset only. A cross-validation fold method also exists.

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: Supervised classification: accuracy, MCC, AUROC and AUPRC, macro-averaged over labels for multi-label tasks. Zero-shot SNV tasks add embedding cosine similarity AUROC and AUPRC and masked log-likelihood ratio AUROC and AUPRC. The README says regression tasks exist but the files read do not list their metrics. Higher is better for all the metrics listed.

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: None described: splits are inherited from the wrapped benchmarks and the README does not mention identity cut-offs, time splits or held-out families.

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: No replicates, seeds or intervals are required. The README notes that num_workers greater than 0 can make results non-deterministic on several tasks and recommends keeping num_workers at 0 for reproducibility.

facts.value: A DNA sequence with a label for classification tasks, or a variant and reference sequence pair with a label for variant effect tasks; the LRB enhancer and histone mark tasks score genomic bins.

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: Zero-shot, linear probing (backbone frozen, projection layer trained) and full fine-tuning are all supported. Full fine-tuning must run in the same process as the model; linear probing can keep the backbone in a separate environment.

notes: The accompanying preprint was not fetched today: the only open copy is the bioRxiv PDF at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.02.19.706811v2.full.pdf, and bioRxiv was rate-limiting this address, so this page is written from the official repository (NVIDIA/GFMBench-api) alone and coverage is limited. The repository lists 22 tasks; the store holds 37 protocols and 20 datasets for this record, so some store protocols (the zs-ar-llr, zs-mlm-llr and zs-embedding variants of the same task) are scoring modes rather than separate tasks. AUROC is given as the primary metric for every entry except IndelClinvarTask and LoleveCausalEqtlTask, because it is the one metric computed for both the supervised and the zero-shot SNV families in the base classes read; those two indel tasks are not SNV tasks and their base class was not read, so their metric is null; the library also computes accuracy, MCC and AUPRC. size is null throughout: the files read give no example counts. data_url is null because each task downloads its data from the original benchmark's own address, listed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, which was not fetched. The repository README cites the paper's own description of the tasks; task names here are the repository's class names, which differ from the store's protocol names. The repository address https://github.com/NVIDIA/GFMBench-api, used as code_url and in the clone step, is the address the three saved files were fetched from (raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/GFMBench-api at commit 55723dcefae91293fe6da01106857ddb1cbf9ab6); no saved file prints it.
